Nature, Published online: 13 August 2025; doi:10.1038/d41586-025-02539-1

A humidity index has been developed that considers lateral flow along rivers and groundwater systems, as well as precipitation, potential evaporation and plant transpiration. It performs better than a conventional humidity index when describing water availability for ecosystems and societies in arid regions.

title: Air pollution could be reduced by incentivizing local government officials to control crop burning
summary:
Nature, Published online: 13 August 2025; doi:10.1038/d41586-025-02545-3

Crop-residue burning in South Asia decreases by up to 14.5% when smoke from fires would affect bureaucrats’ home districts instead of neighbouring ones. Bureaucratic action to punish farmers deters future fires by a further 13%. Thus, using administrator incentives to control crop burning could guide policy towards improving air quality and reducing infant and child mortality.

title: Host and environmental determinants of human milk oligosaccharides and microbiota in the Lifelines NEXT cohort
summary: Spreckels et al. study human milk oligosaccharides and milk microbiota in Lifelines NEXT families. Human milk has an individual-specific composition, which is affected by maternal genetics, lactation stage, subclinical mastitis, and different feeding practices. Specific milk components associate with early infant gut microbiota composition and, potentially, infant growth and eczema.

summary: Insect antiviral factors that specifically target and degrade viral capsids remain largely unknown. Du et al. discover that insect Toll-pathway-mediated broad-spectrum antiviral GTPase myxovirus resistance-like proteins form biomolecular condensates to trap viral capsid proteins along with E3 ubiquitin ligase, thereby promoting ubiquitinated degradation of viral capsids.

title: Caveolin-1/PPARα axis suppresses T follicular helper cell response in primary Sjögren disease
summary: Yu et al. show that the caveolin-1/PPARα axis represses Icos transcription in mouse and human pathogenic T follicular helper (Tfh) cells. Targeting this pathway with clinically available PPARα agonists such as fenofibrate has the potential to ameliorate Sjögren disease and potentially other antibody-mediated autoimmune disorders.

title: Clonal expansion and diversification of germinal center and memory B cell responses to booster immunization in primates
summary: Deimel et al. evaluate the memory B cell and germinal center (GC) response to booster immunization in rhesus macaques. Unlike murine models, the large memory compartment in primates was found to actively participate in booster GCs, including the seeding of new distal sites upon contralateral immunization.

title: Targeting fibroblast TNF receptor 1 attenuates type 17 skin inflammation
summary: Cavagnero et al. use experimental and computational approaches to identify TNF signaling in immune-acting fibroblasts as a key driver of type 17 skin inflammation. Their findings explain how therapeutic blockade of TNF treats inflammatory skin diseases and challenge the current view that TNF acts primarily through keratinocytes.

title: Circadian clocks and periodic anticipated fasting prevent fasting-associated hepatic steatosis in calorie restriction
summary: Ebeigbe et al. show that caloric restriction and fasting differentially reprogram gene expression and fat metabolism in the liver. Caloric restriction reduces the accumulation of lipid droplets through mechanisms dependent on the circadian clock and entrained anticipation of fasting.

title: A comprehensive atlas of the bonobo gut bacteriome and its associated host and exposome factors
summary: This resource encompasses 644 gut bacteriome profiles from 212 wild and zoo-housed bonobos with associated data on 104 host and exposome factors. Leveraging this resource, Torfs et al. reveal key influential factors of the bonobo gut bacteriome, such as lifestyle, diet, maternal kinship, and a strong effect of social contact.

title: Insect dome receptor directly recognizes viral envelopes to activate JAK/STAT signaling and induce conserved antiviral viperin expression
summary: Insect JAK/STAT signaling is crucial for antiviral defense, yet its activation by arboviruses is unclear. Chen et al. reveal that RGDV uses its outer capsid protein P8 to activate the Dome receptor, initiating JAK/STAT signaling and viperin expression, while the virus inhibits this response via its protein Pns11.

title: Signatures of omicron-like adaptation in early SARS-CoV-2 variants and chronic infection
summary: Cheng et al. report SARS-CoV-2 evasion of neutralizing antibodies against the spike protein’s fusion peptide region within an immune-compromised host, resulting in dramatic loss of spike-mediated fusogenicity. This mirrors the immune evasion and loss of fusogenicity of the highly successful but less pathogenic Omicron BA.1 variant.

title: PARP7 inhibition stabilizes STAT1/STAT2 and relieves experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis in mice
summary: The regulation of type I interferon signaling is essential for fine-tuning innate immunity against infections, cancer, and autoimmunity. Xu et al. uncover how PARP7 suppresses this pathway through mono-ADP-ribosylation of STAT1/STAT2, leading to their degradation. Inhibiting PARP7 restores interferon activity, offering a potential therapeutic approach for multiple sclerosis.

title: 53BP1 regulates p53-E2F7-dependent transcriptional gene repression and participates in the Fanconi anemia pathway
summary: Fu et al. revealed that H4K20me2 facilitated the recruitment of 53BP1 on E2F7 TSS in unstressed cells. 53BP1 could inhibit p53 binding on E2F7 TSS through modulating epigenetic modifications status. 53BP1 depletion led to p53-E2F7 upregulation and FANC genes downregulation, which promoted the cellular sensitivity to ICLs.

title: Early time window for memory ensemble allocation specifically depending on activity in Syt2+ early-born parvalbumin interneurons
summary: Valbuena et al. investigate how parvalbumin (PV) and principal neuron (PN) subpopulations affect hippocampal memory formation and consolidation. They show that Syt2+PV+ interneurons are required during an early time window to allocate the proper PN subpopulation to forming memory ensembles, whereas Syt2−/PV+ are required subsequently to consolidate and retrieve memories.
authors: Sergio Valbuena, Komal Bhandari, Annapoorani Udhayachandran, Matteo Tripodi, Pico Caroni

title: High-speed voltage imaging of action potentials in molecular layer interneurons reveals sensory-driven synchrony that augments movement
summary: Brown et al. demonstrate methods for large-scale voltage imaging of inhibitory interneurons in the cerebellum of awake mice. Optical voltage recordings show that sensory input synchronizes interneurons on a millisecond timescale, with synchronization covarying with movement. Briefly photostimulating interneurons drives movement, suggesting a causal role of synchrony in motor control.
authors: Spencer T. Brown, Meghana R. Holla, Michelle A. Land, Shuyuan Yang, Alex J. McDonald, François St-Pierre, Indira M. Raman
